findings.mechanism: Static HashMap ORDERS_BY_ID gets an entry for every new order via store() (OrderCache.java:122, called from OrderService.java:167). Nothing but the test-only invalidateAll() ever removes or evicts entries, and there is no size or TTL bound, so the map is a GC root that grows with every distinct order id.
findings.cause: Unbounded idempotency cache. Each entry keeps the whole Order alive: its line list, the Line records and the per-order notes string (about 200 chars, unique per request). Retries only ever repeat requests from a few moments earlier, so old entries are never read again.
findings.evidence: Ran ./build.sh run 20000. After System.gc() at each checkpoint, cached orders and heap in use rose in step: 4375 orders/3913 KB, 8750/6363 KB, 13125/8915 KB, 17500/11338 KB. That is about 0.6 KB per cached order, linear, and it never drops after a GC. Cache size equals the number of placed (non-replayed) orders.
findings.discriminator: Live set after a full GC grows linearly with the number of distinct orders placed, and OrderCache.size() grows by the same count. Fix: bound the cache (LRU or max size, or a TTL covering the retry window).
